MUQATIL:18:38-41/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:38-41/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:38-41/r2.claim: The believer rebukes the garden owner for not saying that the garden exists by God's will and without power of his own.

MUQATIL:18:38-41/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:38-41/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:38-41/r3.claim: The believer answers that he may see him as having less wealth and children.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r3.claim: The particle lawlā means 'why did you not say' that all depends on God's will and power; the believer contrasts his lesser wealth and children with the other's.

FARRA:v2p145/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p145/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p145/r1.claim: In إن ترن أنا أقل منك, أنا is a strengthening pronoun when أقل is accusative and a noun when أقل is nominative; both readings are valid.

TUSTARI:18:39/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:39/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:39/r1.claim: What God willed refers to His pre-eternal knowledge, which no one knows but God.

TUSTARI:18:39/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:39/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:39/r2.claim: The declaration of having no power except through God means people cannot fulfill the original command, remain safe from its consequences, or reach a good end without divine help.

TUSTARI:18:39/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:39/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:39/r3.claim: Sahl glosses the prophetic formula as having no escape from ignorance at the root or persistence in its branches except through God’s protection, nor power to obey except through His help.

TUSTARI:18:39/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:39/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:39/r4.claim: The best gift to a servant is knowledge that makes him grow in dependence on God.

TAB-FULL:v15p264/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p264/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p264/r1.claim: The garden’s owner should have said that what God willed had happened when he entered and admired it; the conditional response, that it happened, is omitted but understood.

TAB-FULL:v15p264/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p264/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p264/r2.claim: On this parsing, ما is accusative as the object of شاء, and the answer to the conditional is understood though unspoken.

TAB-FULL:v15p264/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p264/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p264/r3.claim: Another Arabist parses ما as nominative with هو understood, yielding the sense it is what God willed.

TAB-FULL:v15p264/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p264/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p264/r4.claim: لا قوة إلا بالله means that one has no ability to carry out the sought obedience except through God.

TAB-FULL:v15p265/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p265/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p265/r1.claim: The line إن ترن انا أقل منك is spoken by the poor believer to the garden’s wealthy owner; the believer is compared to Salmān, Ṣuhayb, and Khabbāb.

TAB-FULL:v15p265/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p265/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p265/r2.claim: When أنا is an inserted supporting pronoun, أقل is accusative; this is the reading adopted by the regional readers and al-Ṭabarī.

TAB-FULL:v15p265/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p265/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p265/r3.claim: If أنا is instead treated as the subject, then أقل takes the nominative.

ZAJJAJ:v3p288#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p288#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p288#2/r1.claim: لا قوة is preferably accusative as absolute negation; nominative is possible and means no one has power except through God.

ZAJJAJ:v3p288#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p288#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p288#2/r2.claim: In إن ترني, أقل is the second object; أنا can emphasize the pronoun or be a separator, and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read أقل as predicate of أنا.

ZAJJAJ:v3p288/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p288/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p288/r3.claim: Janna means an orchard and lawla means هلا as a rebuke; ما may mean the matter is what God wills or be conditional with an omitted consequence.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr retains the final yāʾ in the listed forms in both connection and pause, which the author calls the original analogical form.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr retain yāʾ in connection for their listed forms, add المهتدي, and omit it at pauses because these endings resemble rhyme.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamzah omit these yāʾs in both connection and pause; in connection they also omit yāʾ in non-rhyme forms such as يوم يأت.

THALABI:v6p170#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p170#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p170#2/r1.claim: The wealthy garden owner, identified as Fatrus, shows his Muslim companion the garden and assumes it will never perish; he doubts the Hour and expects a better return if raised.

THALABI:v6p170#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p170#2/r10.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v6p170#2/r10.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that whoever admires something and says 'What God wills; there is no power except through God' will not be harmed by it.

THALABI:v6p170#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p170#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p170#2/r8.claim: The companion confesses that he does not associate anyone with his Lord.

THALABI:v6p170#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p170#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p170#2/r9.claim: In ma sha'a Allah, ma may be nominative as 'it is what God wills' or accusative as the object of 'willed'; an omitted consequence can mean what God wills occurs and what He does not will cannot.

THALABI:v6p171/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p171/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p171/r1.claim: In the phrase إن ترن أنا, أنا is an emphatic pronoun functioning as the subject, hence nominative.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p21#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p21#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p21#2/r1.claim: “If only, when you entered your garden” is a rebuke, equivalent to “Why did you not?”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p21#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p21#2/r2.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p21#2/r2.claim: One parse makes “what” a nominative subject: the matter is what God wills; this rebuts the unbelieving owner's claim that his garden would never perish.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p21#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p21#2/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p21#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, “what” is the object of “wills” in a conditional phrase; the answer “whatever God wills occurs” is omitted but understood, as in the verse about seeking a tunnel through the earth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r1.claim: No one can keep the property and blessing in his hands except through God, and a person has only what God wills.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the believer then turned back to himself before saying he had less wealth and children.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r3.claim: With “less” accusative, “I” is an emphatic separator; with “less” nominative, “I” is a noun; both readings are permissible.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p22/r4.claim: “I” can emphasize the attached first-person pronoun or serve as a separator; “less” can be accusative as the second object of “you see” or nominative as its subject's predicate.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:37-41/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:37-41/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:37-41/r3.claim: The believer rebukes the garden owner for failing to acknowledge God's will and teaches him to say that his possession and power exist only by God.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:37-41/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:37-41/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:37-41/r4.claim: The believer hopes God may grant him something better in this world or the next and send a heavenly calamity upon the garden.

JISHUMI:v6p4413/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r1.claim: Those devoted to worldly life and those seeking their Lord's approval each end in the outcome they deserve.

JISHUMI:v6p4413/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r10.claim: Arabic allows several forms of لكن هو الله, including the uncontracted original لكن أنا الله.

JISHUMI:v6p4413/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r2.claim: Worldly enjoyment does not last, so people should not be deceived by it.

JISHUMI:v6p4413/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r3.claim: The passage demonstrates the falsity of conjecture.

JISHUMI:v6p4413/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r7.claim: The man owns his deeds and statements, including his wrongdoing, which is therefore attributed to him.

JISHUMI:v6p4413/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r8.speaker: ابن عامر، ابن كثير، نافع، يعقوب
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r8.claim: These readers pronounce لكنا with an alif when continuing; the others omit it and double the n, while all retain the alif at pause.

JISHUMI:v6p4413/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r9.claim: The form derives from لكن أنا هو; hamza deletion and assimilation explain the connected readings and variation in retaining أنا's alif.

JISHUMI:v6p4415/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4415/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4415/r8.claim: One grammatical analysis makes ما شاء الله a conditional expression with an understood إنما; another makes it an object of شاء.

JISHUMI:v6p4415/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4415/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4415/r9.claim: إن ترن أنا أقل منك مالا means إن ترني أقل; أنا is attached after إن.

JISHUMI:v6p4419/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4419/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4419/r3.claim: When seeing a blessing, one should thank God, rely on Him, and recognize the blessing as from His power; this helps it endure.

JISHUMI:v6p4419/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4419/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4419/r4.claim: The accountable person's foremost concern should be the bliss of the afterlife.

JISHUMI:v6p4419/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4419/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4419/r6.claim: Disbelief and associating partners with God are human acts for which people are blamed, refuting the Mujabira.

JISHUMI:v6p4419/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4419/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4419/r7.claim: The man could have said ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله; reproaching him for omission entails that capacity precedes the act.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r5.claim: Mā shāʾ Allāh may mean that the matter is as God wills; an unspoken completion is that what God wills comes to be.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r6.claim: There is no power to preserve one's wealth or repel harm except by God's permission.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r7.speaker: هشام بن عروة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r7.claim: He reports that his father would say the phrase when admiring his wealth or entering one of his gardens.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r8.claim: Anā is emphatic support and explains the accusative aqalla; the believer means his companion is arrogant if he sees himself as richer.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r1.claim: “Whatever God wills” can be a relative clause, with the omitted predicate “the matter is,” or a conditional with omitted result, “whatever God wills comes to pass.”

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r2.claim: On entering the garden, one should acknowledge that its existence and every good in it depend on God’s will and grace, and that He can preserve or ruin it.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r3.claim: “There is no strength except through God” confesses that cultivation and management depend on divine support; bodily ability and property are not independent of Him.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r4.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r4.claim: ʿUrwa used to open a breach in his garden wall during the date harvest, invite visitors, and repeat this verse while inside.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r5.claim: With accusative “aqalla,” ana is an emphatic separator; with nominative, ana is the subject and aqallu its predicate, and the clause is the second object of tarani.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675#3/r6.claim: “Children” supports understanding nufar in 18:34 as offspring; the believer expects God may reverse their fortunes, granting him a better garden for faith and ruining the other man’s garden for disbelief.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r1.claim: The believer's lawla is an exhortation meaning why did you not say this when entering your garden?

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r2.claim: Ma shāʾ Allāh can be a relative clause, a condition, or a report with an omitted subject such as the matter is what God willed.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r3.claim: La quwwata illa billah expresses surrender and opposes the unbeliever's claim that his garden will never perish.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r4.claim: The Prophet taught Abu Hurayra la quwwata illa billah as a treasure from Paradise and says God calls the speaker His surrendered servant.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r5.speaker: أبو موسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r5.claim: A report to Abu Musa gives the fuller formula la hawla wa la quwwata illa billahi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿazim as a treasure of Paradise.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir retains the yā in tarani in both connected and paused reading; Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamza omit it in both.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r7.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r7.claim: Nafi and Abu Amr retain the yā in connection only.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r8.claim: The majority read aqalla in the accusative as the second object, with ana as an inserted separator.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r9.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518/r9.claim: Isa b. Umar reads aqallu in the nominative, making ana the subject and aqallu its predicate; the vision here is inward.

TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r3.claim: The vocalized form غورا can be a dialect equivalent of غور and a verbal noun placed where an adjective would normally stand for emphasis.

TABRISI:18:39-42/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:39-42/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:39-42/r1.claim: The poor believer says his companion should have thanked God on entering the garden: its fruits and crops exist by God's will and power, and God could remove its blessing.

TABRISI:18:39-42/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:39-42/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:39-42/r2.claim: Although now poorer in wealth, family, and children, the believer hopes God may give him a better garden in this world or the next.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r1.claim: The opening is a reproach: why did you not say this when you entered your garden?

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r2.claim: ما شاء الله can be parsed with an implied هو, meaning this is what God willed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r3.claim: Alternatively, an implied كان gives the sense that whatever God willed came to pass; the response to the conditional may be omitted when understood.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r4.claim: He prefers لا قوة إلا بالله in the accusative without nunation, as a total negation like لا ريب فيها.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r5.claim: It may also be nominative, with لا قوة as subject and بالله as predicate; no one has bodily or material power except by God and only what He wills occurs.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r6.claim: He reads إن ترني أنا and يؤتيني with yāʾ in both connected and paused forms.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r7.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r7.claim: They retain the yāʾ in connected reading.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r8.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r8.claim: They omit the yāʾ in both forms, in connected and paused recitation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r9.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p144/r9.claim: He reads أنا أقل with lām in the nominative; al-Farra says أنا is an emphatic element when أقل is accusative but a subject when أقل is nominative, and both readings are valid.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r1.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r1.claim: Al-Qaffal reads ما شاء الله as referring to the things visibly present in the garden, as in examples where a phrase points to an existing object.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r10.claim: With أقل read in the nominative, أنا is the subject and أقل its predicate, with the clause as the second object of ترى.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r11.claim: The mention of children shows that the earlier word نفرا includes helpers and offspring.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r12.claim: The believer says that if he has less wealth, children, and worldly supporters, his Lord may give him something better in this world or the next.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r2.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r2.claim: On al-Qaffal's reading, only the garden's observed objects are said to have been willed into existence; the claim is not universal.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r3.claim: Razi judges al-Qaffal's explanation much better than the answers offered by al-Jubba'i and al-Ka'bi.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r4.claim: Even al-Qaffal's answer leaves the Mu'tazili difficulty: the garden may have been built through theft and grave injustice, which cannot be attributed to God's will on their doctrine.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r5.claim: Restricting God's will to the fruit's growth would narrow the text's apparent scope without evidence.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r6.claim: No one has power over any matter except through God's aid and empowerment.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r7.claim: The believer tells the owner to acknowledge that the garden and its good are from God's will and grace, and God can preserve or ruin it.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r8.claim: He should also acknowledge that his ability to build and manage the garden depends on God's support; no one has bodily or material strength apart from Him.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r9.claim: With أقل read in the accusative, أنا is a separator pronoun and أقل is the second object of ترى.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r10.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r10.claim: Al-Ka'bi also accepts that things forbidden by God may still occur within His dominion despite not being willed.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r11.claim: Razi says al-Ka'bi's reply concedes a violation of the verse's apparent meaning and wrongly equates divine willing with divine commands.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r2.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r2.claim: Al-Qaffal says the believer denies association because he sees poverty and wealth as God's dispensation, thanking Him for gifts, showing patience in trials, and refusing pride.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r3.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r3.claim: The wealthy unbeliever's self-attribution of status and riches effectively makes a partner with God in granting honor and affluence.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r4.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r4.claim: The believer may be answering an idolater who denied resurrection by rejecting the worship of idols and affirming God's uniqueness.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r5.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r5.claim: By claiming God cannot resurrect, the unbeliever makes God equal to created beings in incapacity and thereby posits a partner.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r6.claim: The believer instructs the garden owner to say ما شاء الله; ما may be conditional with an omitted result, meaning whatever God wills comes to pass.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r7.claim: Alternatively, ما is a relative pronoun serving as the predicate of an omitted subject: the matter is what God willed.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r8.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r8.claim: Asharites infer that everything God wills occurs and what He does not will does not occur, so God did not will the unbeliever's faith, against the Mu'tazila.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r9.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v21p108/r9.claim: Al-Ka'bi answers that the phrase concerns what God directly does, not human acts, comparing it with the claim that God's command cannot be nullified.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:39-40/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39-40/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39-40/r7.claim: In the conditional sentence, tara is jussive and fa-ʿasa is the answer; ana is parenthetical, or may emphasize the first-person pronoun as an object.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:39-40/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39-40/r8.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39-40/r8.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads ana with nominative case as a subject and aqalla as its predicate; the phrase is the second object, and retaining the yāʾ is good and original though its deletion is indicated by the kasra.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r1.claim: The believer rebukes and advises his companion: when entering the garden he should have said the words with his heart; the garden exists by God’s will, not his own power.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r2.speaker: الزجاج والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj and al-Farra explain the declaration as saying that the affair itself is what God wills.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r3.claim: An alternative supplies the omitted answer: what God wills comes to be and what He does not will cannot be.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r4.claim: The wealth gathered in the garden came through God’s power, who could have removed its blessing; it was not the owner’s independent strength.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r5.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r5.claim: Malik says anyone entering his home ought to say these words.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r6.speaker: ابن وهب
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r6.claim: Ibn Wahb says Hafs ibn Maysara saw the phrase written over Wahb ibn Munabbih’s door.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r7.claim: The Prophet taught Abu Musa that la hawla wa-la quwwata illa bi-llah is a treasure of Paradise; Muslim records the report in his Sahih with wording variants.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:39/r8.claim: A report recommends saying in God’s name and acknowledging His will and power on entering or leaving home, saying this drives devils away and brings blessings; Aisha explains the angel’s responses as guidance, sufficiency, and protection.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r1.claim: The garden owner should have said this on entering: whatever God wills will be, whether He preserves or destroys it; the phrase admits several syntactic readings.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r2.claim: Saying there is no power except through God acknowledges personal incapacity and God's power, including the ability to cultivate and manage the garden.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r3.claim: The Prophet says that whoever sees something pleasing and says these words will not be harmed by it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:39/r4.claim: In you see me, ana may be an emphatic separator or an object emphasis; ولد can support interpreting nafar as children.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r1.claim: “What God wills” may be a nominal clause meaning that the matter is God's will, or a conditional phrase whose consequence is implicit: whatever God wills occurs.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r2.claim: The garden owner should have acknowledged that its prosperity depended on God's will and that God could preserve or ruin it.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r3.claim: “There is no power except through God” acknowledges that his ability to cultivate and manage the garden came from divine aid.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r4.claim: When “I” is followed by accusative “less,” it is a separator; with nominative “less” in al-Kisāʾī's reading, “I” is subject and the clause is the second object of taranī.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#5/r5.claim: The mention of offspring supports interpreting nafar in the earlier story as children.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p175/r8.claim: The companion apparently also had wealth and followers, contrary to historical reports that he was a destitute petitioner; the comparison in the text supports this reading.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r10.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r10.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads aqallu nominative, making anā the subject and aqallu its predicate or a circumstantial clause depending on the verb's sense.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r11.claim: The reference to offspring indicates that the earlier boast about greater nafr meant children if it is contrasted with fewer children.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r4.claim: The advice ma shāʾ Allāh acknowledges that all things happen by God's will, who may impoverish, enrich, support, or forsake anyone.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r5.claim: Mā can be conditional, with an omitted result meaning whatever God wills comes to pass, or relative as subject or predicate; lawlā is exhortative and separated from its verb by an adverbial.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r6.claim: The companion counsels him to disown personal power in his affairs and acknowledge that power belongs to God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r7.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r7.claim: The Prophet tells Abū Hurayra that lā quwwata illā billāh is a word from Paradise's treasure; God says the speaker has submitted. A similar report from Abū Mūsā adds al-ʿAliyy al-ʿAẓīm.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r8.claim: The believer expects God to give him a better garden for his faith, remove the unbeliever's favor for disbelief, and ruin his garden.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r9.claim: The majority read aqalla in the accusative as the second object of taranī in a knowledge construction; an alternative analyzes it as a circumstantial accusative with anā emphasizing the object.

SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r1.claim: إلا بالله is the predicate of لا التبرئة, and the whole phrase is also an object of قلت, alongside ما شاء الله.

SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r2.claim: أنا may emphasize the speaker's yāʾ or separate the two objects; أقل is a second object or circumstantial according to whether ترن means see or know. If seeing, أنا can only be emphasis.

SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r3.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r3.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads أقل in the nominative, making أنا the topic and أقل its predicate.

SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:39#2/r4.claim: مالا وولدا are accusative specifications, and فعسى ربي is the response to the conditional clause.

SAMIN-DURR:18:39/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:39/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:39/r1.claim: لولا is an exhortation governing قلت; إذ دخلت is attached to قلت and interrupts between لولا and its complement without being foreign, while a past verb after exhortation expresses rebuke.

SAMIN-DURR:18:39/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:39/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:39/r2.claim: ما شاء الله may be conditional, with ما as a necessarily fronted object and an omitted response meaning that whatever God willed occurred.

SAMIN-DURR:18:39/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:39/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:39/r3.claim: Alternatively, ما may be relative: either a topic with omitted predicate, or the predicate of an implicit topic; the sentence is governed by قلت.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r3.claim: The garden owner should have praised God on seeing what delighted him, acknowledging that God granted him exceptional wealth and children and that there is no power except through God.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r4.claim: Some early authorities advise saying God willing, no power except through God when impressed by one's condition, possessions, or children, deriving the counsel from this verse.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r5.claim: A report from Anas says that when a servant says God willing, no power except through God, over a blessing of family, wealth, or children, he will see no calamity in it short of death; Abu Ya'la transmits it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r1.speaker: أبو الفتح الأزدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r1.claim: Al-Azdi says the Anas report through Isa ibn Awn and Abd al-Malik ibn Zarara is not sound.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r2.claim: The Prophet called the phrase no power except through God a treasure from the Garden; Ahmad alone transmits this report.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r3.claim: In an authentic report to Abu Musa, the Prophet calls there is no might or power except through God a treasure of the Garden.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p159/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra distinguishes the treasure under the Throne as the phrase no power except through God, and says this is the wording in the Cave verse, unlike no might or power except through God.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r4.claim: The believer teaches the garden owner to remember God’s will on entering, echoing the instruction not to assert certainty about future events.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r5.claim: “What God wills” covers what He wills in the present and future, whether already manifest or still to come; the response is left unstated for that breadth.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r6.claim: “There is no power except through God” affirms God’s power and the servant’s disavowal of independent power, and teaches that created capacity depends on His determination.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r7.claim: The phrase also refutes philosophers who treat natural properties as independently effective.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p469/r8.claim: The believer acknowledges having less wealth and children, the latter being a person’s dearest dependents, unlike the other man’s boastful pride.

DURR-FULL:v5p391/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r1.speaker: ابن شهاب
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r1.claim: Ibn Shihab recited ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله when entering his properties, applying the verse about entering one's garden.

DURR-FULL:v5p391/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r10.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r10.claim: The Prophet also described لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله as a treasure of Paradise.

DURR-FULL:v5p391/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r2.speaker: مالك
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r2.claim: Malik said ما شاء الله when entering his home, citing the verse as his reason.

DURR-FULL:v5p391/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r3.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih had ما شاء الله written on his door, following this verse.

DURR-FULL:v5p391/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r4.speaker: عمر بن مرة
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r4.claim: Umar ibn Murrah says one of the best prayers is a person's saying ما شاء الله.

DURR-FULL:v5p391/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r5.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r5.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham says no request succeeds more than one made by saying ما شاء الله.

DURR-FULL:v5p391/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r6.speaker: موسى
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r6.claim: When Moses's request was delayed, he said ما شاء الله and found it granted; God told him this is the most successful word for asking needs.

DURR-FULL:v5p391/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r7.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r7.claim: The Prophet described لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله as a gate among the gates of Paradise.

DURR-FULL:v5p391/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r8.speaker: قيس بن سعد بن عبادة
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r8.claim: The Prophet taught Qays ibn Sa'd, after he had served him, that لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله is a gate of Paradise.

DURR-FULL:v5p391/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v5p391/r9.claim: The Prophet called this remembrance a word from the treasure of Paradise when teaching it to Abu Dharr.

DURR-FULL:v5p392/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r1.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r1.claim: The Prophet instructed Abu Ayyub to say لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله often because it is a treasure of Paradise.

DURR-FULL:v5p392/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r2.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r2.claim: The Prophet encouraged frequent recitation of لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله as a treasure of Paradise.

DURR-FULL:v5p392/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r3.claim: The Prophet described لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله as a treasure of Paradise.

DURR-FULL:v5p392/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r4.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r4.claim: A person whose family, property, or children receive God's blessing can ward off calamity until death by saying ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله, as the Prophet applied this verse.

DURR-FULL:v5p392/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r5.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r5.claim: Anas says that saying the formula upon admiring one's property protects it from harm, and he cites the garden verse.

DURR-FULL:v5p392/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r6.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits the preceding protection report from Anas as a prophetic narration.

DURR-FULL:v5p392/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r7.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r7.claim: The Prophet advised repeating لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله to preserve a blessing, then recited the verse about entering one's garden.

DURR-FULL:v5p392/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r8.claim: A report calls لا قوة إلا بالله a treasure beneath the Throne; Abu Hurayra corrected a listener that this wording belongs to the Cave verse.

DURR-FULL:v5p392/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r9.speaker: جرير
DURR-FULL:v5p392/r9.claim: While traveling to Persia, Jarir said the garden formula; a man told him that a spirit posing as his companion had heard the phrase in heaven and was driven away when Jarir repeated it.

DURR-FULL:v5p393/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r1.speaker: جرير
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r1.claim: The spirit shrank to a fly as Jarir repeated ما شاء الله لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله, then said it had learned the phrase and stopped visiting him.

DURR-FULL:v5p393/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r2.speaker: يحيى بن سليم الثقفي
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r2.claim: A teacher told Yahya ibn Sulaym that angels use ما شاء الله to drive away devils trying to overhear heaven.

DURR-FULL:v5p393/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r3.speaker: صفوان بن سليم
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r3.claim: Safwan says no angel rises from earth without saying لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله.

DURR-FULL:v5p393/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r4.claim: The Prophet called لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله a remedy for ninety-nine ailments, the least of them worry.

DURR-FULL:v5p393/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r5.claim: Gabriel explained the formula as having no ability to avoid God's disobedience except through Him and no strength to obey except through His aid.

DURR-FULL:v5p393/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says obedience is possible only through God's power and abandoning disobedience only through Him.

DURR-FULL:v5p393/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r7.speaker: زهير بن محمد
DURR-FULL:v5p393/r7.claim: Zuhayr explains the formula as being able to take what one loves only through God and refrain from what one dislikes only through His aid.

BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r1.claim: The omitted predicate is that the matter is as God wills; the phrase urges acknowledgment that He may preserve or ruin the garden and all it contains.

BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r2.claim: Saying there is no power except through God admits human incapacity and that cultivating and managing the garden depended on divine aid and enabling.

BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r3.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r3.claim: A report says that one who admires something and says this remembrance will be protected from the evil eye.

BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r4.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r4.claim: A report says that someone who sees another granted family or wealth and says this remembrance will see no harm in it.

BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r5.claim: The Prophet explains that avoiding disobedience requires God's protection, while strength to obey comes only from Him.

BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r6.speaker: رُوي
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r6.claim: A report calls this remembrance a remedy for ninety-nine ailments, the least of them worry.

BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p191#2/r7.claim: The original wording is أن ترني; أقل is either a circumstantial accusative with visual seeing or the second object of cognitive seeing, and أنا reinforces the omitted first-person pronoun.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r1.claim: The opening لولا rebukes the garden-owner and urges him to say this at the very moment of entering.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r10.speaker: عمرو بن مرة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r10.claim: Ibn Murra says that a person’s saying ما شاء الله is among the best supplications.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r11.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r11.claim: Anas reports a Prophetic promise that invoking the phrase over blessings in family, property, or children protects from every calamity until death.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r2.claim: ما شاء الله may mean “the matter is what God wills,” or “whatever God willed has come to be”; it can be a relative or a conditional clause.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r3.claim: Either construction urges recognition that the orchard and everything in it exist by God’s will and may be preserved or destroyed by Him.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r4.claim: If ما is conditional or functions like one, the wording also implies that what God does not will will not occur.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r5.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r5.claim: The Muʿtazilite al-Qaffal restricts “what God willed” to the fruit in the garden, denying that the clause is universal.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r6.speaker: الكعبي والجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r6.claim: Al-Kaʿbi and al-Jubbaʾi say the verse covers only what God directly does, not human acts; things He dislikes may occur in His dominion.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r7.claim: The author insists that the natural reading is universal and says the Muʿtazilites depart from that sense to protect their doctrine.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r8.claim: “There is no power except through God” confesses the speaker’s inability and that his building and management depend on divine aid and empowerment.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p279#2/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s description of this invocation as a treasure of Paradise beneath the Throne; he distinguishes it from لا حول ولا قوة بالله.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r1.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r1.claim: Anas says that invoking the phrase when something in one’s property pleases the viewer prevents calamity from striking it; another version is Prophetic.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r2.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r2.claim: Malik said ما شاء الله when entering his home, citing the verse; Ibn al-ʿArabi inferred that it is recommended when entering one’s home.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r3.speaker: عروة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r3.claim: ʿUrwa said the phrase on seeing something pleasing in his property or entering a garden, applying the verse.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r4.claim: Reports support saying the invocation on seeing anything pleasing, one’s own or another’s, as protection from the evil eye of admiration.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r5.claim: In ترني أنا أقل, أنا emphasizes the object pronoun; تراني may denote knowledge, taking أقل as its second object, or sight, making it a circumstantial phrase.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r6.claim: أنا can instead be a separator, in which case the seeing verb must be cognitive rather than visual.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r7.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r7.claim: Isa ibn ʿUmar reads أقل in the nominative; أنا is then the subject and أقل its predicate.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p280/r8.claim: مالا وولدا are specification words on both readings.

ELMALILI:18:32-44/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:32-44/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:32-44/r1.claim: The garden's owner is told he should have said “What God wills; there is no strength except through God” when entering it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p322/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p322/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p322/r7.claim: Walawlā is conjoined to the earlier denial as another censure; before entering the garden he should have said what God willed and that power belongs only to God, not boasted.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324#2/r1.claim: The reply answers the boast of greater wealth and supporters in 18:34: fortunes can shrink or disappear, while a poor person can become wealthy.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324#2/r2.claim: The speaker’s yāʾ is omitted after the protective nūn for ease, a common usage.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324#2/r3.claim: Ana is a separating pronoun, so aqalla is accusative as the second object of tara.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r1.claim: One explanation takes mā in mā shāʾ Allāh as a relative pronoun: this garden is what God willed to give me.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers mā as an indefinite noun qualified by the following clause: this is something God willed for me.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r3.claim: No power belongs to the speaker to make the garden; human capacities are gifts from God and operate only with His help through sound means and tools.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p324/r4.claim: The general statement that there is no power except through God explains why the garden is one instance of creation enabled by God-given human powers.

TABATABAI:18:39-40/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:39-40/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:39-40/r1.claim: The believer’s response describes the faithful stance in contrast with the wealthy man’s claim; he should have credited the garden to God’s will and denied independent power.

TABATABAI:18:39-40/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:39-40/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:39-40/r2.claim: “What God wills” may mean the thing God willed or that what He wills exists; a conditional reading is possible, but the first best serves the argument that all affairs depend on God.

TABATABAI:18:39-40/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:39-40/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:39-40/r3.claim: “There is no power except through God” means every created power remains sustained by God and never becomes independent of Him, as 2:165 says all power belongs to God.

ASAD-NOTES:18:39#n46/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:39#n46/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:39#n46/r1.claim: Asad renders law-la as alas and points to his fuller explanation at 10:98.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The particle in the verse separates the two objects of the verb as an auxiliary element, a usage found in classical Arabic and other languages.

QIRAAT-ER:18:39:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:39:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:39:16#1/r1.claim: Retaining the object-pronoun yāʾ adds prosodic lengthening and emphasis to the seeing-me moment.

QIRAAT-ER:18:39:16#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:39:16#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:39:16#2/r1.claim: The pausal taran drops the pronoun vowel, creating a clipped and emphatic conditional.

QIRAAT-ER:18:39:17#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:39:17#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:39:17#1/r1.claim: Short alif reduces anā to a minimal form that may de-emphasize its separating or emphatic function.

QIRAAT-ER:18:39:17#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:39:17#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:39:17#2/r1.claim: Extended madd lengthens the pronoun and strengthens its emphatic or separating force.

STUDYQURAN:18:39/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:39/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:39/r1.claim: Mā shāʾ Allāh recognizes that nothing happens outside God’s will.

STUDYQURAN:18:39/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:39/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:39/r2.claim: Lā quwwata illā bi’Llāh acknowledges that no one accomplishes anything without God’s help.

STUDYQURAN:18:39/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:39/r3.speaker: Ibn Kathīr
STUDYQURAN:18:39/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the verse grounds the custom of saying both formulas when pleased by good fortune; the second is also used amid distress.

STUDYQURAN:18:39/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:39/r4.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:18:39/r4.claim: A hadith identifies the latter formula, or lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā bi’Llāh, as among the treasures of the Garden.
